gap: No result ChatGPT got states that the Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen) are 'not passive' and must be powered on to play over the included AUX cable (Bose's own support article), while Sony's help guide says the WH-1000XM6 plays over its cable even when turned off.
standout_why: Compared against SoundGuys' best-ANC roundup (2026-10-30) and SoundGuys' XM6 vs QC Ultra 2 compare page, both cited by ChatGPT: they cover codecs (Sony SBC/AAC/LDAC/LC3, Bose SBC/AAC/aptX Adaptive), Bose USB-C lossless and Sony's 'No USB listening', but say nothing about what happens over the 3.5 mm cable when the battery is dead or the headset is off. What Hi-Fi's two cited pages would not render for me, so I could not confirm they lack it. ChatGPT's answer pitches Bose as 'especially good for long flights', which is exactly the scenario where this mechanism bites.
decides: Confirms Sony WH-1000XM6 as the safer pick for flights and all-day use: a flat battery still gives wired playback (without ANC) from the seat-back jack. The Bose QC Ultra 2nd Gen has no passive analog path, so a dead battery means silence unless you also plug in USB-C power at the same time, which Bose documents as the workaround. Apple states AirPods Max 2 lossless and low-latency audio require a wired USB-C connection, and Apple's store price is $549, not the $449 ChatGPT showed. Bose's aptX Adaptive/lossless Bluetooth tier only engages on Snapdragon Sound-certified phones, so iPhone users get AAC on both Sony and Bose and the codec difference between them vanishes.

findings.label: Wired (AUX) playback requires power
findings.value: Must be powered on; not passive
findings.source_title: No audio | Bose QuietComfort Ultra Headphones (2nd Gen)
findings.note: Bose wording: 'The headphones are not passive, therefore they must be powered on to work with the AUX cable' and 'In order for this to function, the Headphones must be powered on, even when wired.' Workaround quoted: 'If the battery is depleted, you can use the USB charging cable and the AUX cable at the same time.' Bluetooth is disabled while the cable is connected.

findings.label: Wired playback with headset turned off
findings.value: Works; noise canceling unavailable when off
findings.source_title: WH-1000XM6 Help Guide – Using the supplied headphone cable
findings.note: Sony wording: 'You can listen to music even if the headset is turned off. In this case, the noise canceling function cannot be used.' Also 'When using the headphone cable, the Bluetooth function cannot be used' and the NC/AMB button cannot be used when off. Sony names airplanes as the use case for the cable.
